content.text:
**SR-39385 is a Severity 1 ticket. The 4-hour restoration target was missed by more than twice its length, so Northstar owes Acme a $4,200.00 service credit.** The customer met both of its obligations. Nothing in the record shows the credit was ever decided or issued, and the deadline for that passed on 2026-07-24, so it is now overdue.

**Customer and scope.** The ticket's account is CRM-2048 (Acme Manufacturing). Its DUNS number, 04-812-7730, matches ERP customer C-1001 (Acme Mfg. Holdings). This is not Acme Industrial Supply Co. (CRM-2091), which is a different company and not covered. Acme's support terms are Schedule C to agreement ACME-MFG-2025, on the Platinum plan. They cover NS-500, and coverage started on 2025-04-01. The ticket is in scope.

**True severity: Severity 1 (Critical).** The ticket says the NS-500 controller on stamping line 4 faulted, the line is stopped and there is no workaround. The customer's own "P1" label was not used to decide this.

**Schedule and targets.** The ticket was opened at 2026-06-16 02:14 Central time, so Service Level Schedule v2.0 applies (it covers tickets opened from 2026-04-01). For Severity 1 the targets are a first response within 30 minutes and restoration within 4 hours. The clock runs around the clock and starts when the ticket opens, at 02:14. No pauses are recorded, Northstar asserted no exclusions, and Acme has no maintenance notices on record, so nothing comes off the clock.

**Measurement.**
- **First response: met.** An engineer phoned at 02:31, 17 minutes after opening.
- **Restoration: missed.** Service was restored at 10:58, 8 hours 44 minutes after opening. That is more than twice the 4-hour target, which puts it in the higher of the two credit bands (band 2).

**Credit: $4,200.00.**
- Band 2 earns 20% of the monthly support fee. Acme reported the incident by phone to the Support hotline before restoration, so the higher Severity 1 rate applies.
- The fee for June 2026 is $21,000. The knowledge base read this figure from the contract only loosely, but two March 2026 credits ($3,150 and $420) fit a $21,000 fee.
- 20% of $21,000 is $4,200. The monthly cap is 30%, or $6,300, and no other credits exist for tickets opened in June, so the full amount stands.
- The claim was valid. Edward Floyd, Acme's VP Procurement, emailed a claim naming the ticket on 2026-06-24. The claim window ran to 2026-07-16 23:59 Central time.

**What Northstar owed, and by when** (all times 2026-06-16, Central time):

| Duty | Role | Holder | Latest time |
|---|---|---|---|
| Take over as incident lead | Support Escalation Manager | Hannah Lindqvist | 02:29 |
| Notify | Account owner | Sarah Chen | 02:44 |
| Notify (not restored at 50% of target) | Director of Customer Support | Marcus Adeyemi | 04:14 |
| Notify (not restored at 100% of target) | VP Sales | Michael Torres | 06:14 |
| Notify (Strategic account) | Chief Revenue Officer | David Morgan | 06:14 |
| Decide the claim in writing | Director of Customer Support | Marcus Adeyemi | 2026-07-24 |
| Issue the credit memo against the next support invoice, same day as approval | Support Billing Manager | Paul Brennan | 2026-07-24 |

- The ticket history doesn't record whether any of these engagements or notifications happened. They can't be confirmed as done.
- No root-cause finding is due, because no exclusion was asserted.

**What the customer had to do:**
- **Report by phone to the Support hotline: met.** Johnny Johnson opened the ticket by phone at 02:14, before restoration.
- **Make a timely written claim: met.**
- **Keep a technical contact reachable by phone until restoration: met.** No failed call attempt is recorded.
